title: Reproducibility Project: Psychology — program-level replication estimates for 100 psychology findings
summary: The Reproducibility Project: Psychology is promoted as a program-level replication record rather than a single failed-replication case. The Open Science Collaboration reported replications of 100 experimental and correlational studies from three psychology journals, using high-powered designs and original materials when available. The key archival lesson is not a single percentage of failure: the record preserves multiple replication-success indicators, the observed decline in effect sizes, and the warning that no one indicator is sufficient.

status_cautions: Do not collapse all indicators into a binary failed/succeeded flag.
Do not use the program record as a substitute for child records when asking about a specific original finding.
Interpretation should preserve the possibility of moderators, original false positives, replication false negatives, and inflated original effects.
type_payload.why_it_matters_for_missing_half: It makes the denominator visible: many positive, published findings weakened under independent, planned replication rather than simply disappearing into private skepticism.
